correctness.rationale: For every 0<a<=b, reflection and antipodality reduce angle to [0,pi/2] with density 2/pi. Direct vertex projections give max(cos,a sin)+max(cos,b sin), exactly the stated three branches. Sublevel set lengths of 2cos, M sin(theta+p), and (a+b)sin theta are explicitly intersected with their branch intervals, establishing the CDF at every real threshold and all boundaries. Strict derivative signs prove the b>1, ab<1 third-maximum criterion, exact support endpoints, and the standard quadratic-root density coefficient, with coincident-level qualifications. The standalone checker independently projects vertices, checks 70 parameter sets x51 thresholds x12000 angles, angular means, and critical angle condition; finite tests are supplementary.

value.rationale: The source 2022 paper highlights width-deviation optimization and specifically an asymmetric kite for its remaining quadrilateral case, motivating its full directional-width law. The result gives an explicit all-threshold probability distribution for every Euclidean kite and discovers a sharp geometric transition where its reduced directional profile gains an additional maximum and universal local inverse-square-root peak. This is a complete natural two-parameter geometric classification and distributional benchmark, not a single arbitrarily selected numerical statistic or finite computation. It makes no unsupported claim to solve the original minimization question.
